newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-BESIKTAS IMPOSE RECORD FINE ON MIDFIELDER YALCIN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BESIKTAS IMPOSE RECORD FINE ON MIDFIELDER YALCIN.

text.p: Turkey's Besiktas have imposed a record fine of 30 billion lira ($236,000) on midfielder Sergen Yalcin after he withdrew from the team in a protest over one of the club's directors, Anatolian news agency said on Wednesday.
Former international Sergen said he would not play again unless director Ugur Eksioglu resigned.

"If Ugur Eksioglu doesn't leave the board, from tomorrow I will not turn out for training or for matches. Let him wear the number 10 shirt and play in the Besiktas midfield," Sergen said late on Tuesday.
"I'm 60 years old, I can't wear the team strip but there are many others who can," Eksioglu said later.
Eksioglu said the club could sell Sergen at the end of the season after Besiktas suffered a surprise 4-1 defeat to 10th-placed Samsunspor at the weekend.

"As the board of directors, we have decided that Sergen's action is not just against me but all the board members and we have fined him 30 billion lira ($236,000) and indefinitely suspended him from the team," Eksioglu said after an emergency board meeting on Wednesday.
Besiktas slipped from second to third place after the match with Samsunspor and now lie five points behind leaders Galatasaray.
